title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
keyIdea: The depth of a tree is 1 (the root) plus the deeper of its two subtrees. Ask both children for their depth, take the bigger, add 1. An empty tree has depth 0, so a leaf returns 1.

approaches.name: BFS: count levels
approaches.idea: Walk level by level with a queue; each full level processed adds 1.
approaches.why: Every node is queued once. The queue holds one level at a time, at most the widest level w.

approaches.name: Recursion (post-order)
approaches.idea: NULL → 0. Otherwise lh = maxDepth(left), rh = maxDepth(right), return 1 + max(lh, rh).
approaches.why: One call per node. The call stack is as deep as the tree height h.

quiz.q: What does maxDepth return for a leaf?
options: 1: both NULL children return 0, so 1 + max(0, 0)
A node computes its answer only after both children have returned

quiz.q: Space used by the recursion on a chain of n nodes?
options: O(n): the call stack goes n deep
